# Gemini prompt: TORPEDO ATTACK DATA forms

Start a fresh chat, paste everything between the lines, and attach the
attack forms PDF. Save Gemini's answer exactly as it comes, fences
and all, in the patrol's folder as `attacks-01.md` (a further batch of pages
from the same report goes in `attacks-02.md`). See prompts/README.md for which pages to include.

---

You are transcribing selected pages of a WWII U.S. submarine war patrol
report for a research database. Accuracy is paramount. Never guess,
correct, or normalize the source text. Transcribe only what is on the
pages provided. The pages are a selection, so never infer what the
missing pages might say.

This PDF holds TORPEDO ATTACK DATA forms: for each attack, one page of
target data and one page of torpedo data. These pages are evidence in a
study of torpedo performance, so the exact order and placement of every
value matters as much as the value itself.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Put your whole answer inside one ```text code block so it appears as plain
text with a copy button. After the code block write one line only,
listing anything you could not transcribe.

YOUR TASK — the attack forms (attacks.md)
Transcribe each form page verbatim, as plain text, line for line. Do not
turn the forms into tables.

- Put `### Torpedo attack data, attack <n>` above the target-data page and
  `### Torpedo data, attack <n>` above the torpedo-data page, where <n> is
  the attack number as a numeral (TORPEDO ATTACK NO. TWO is 2), then a line
  `Page <n>` with the page number typed on that page.
- Keep the time, zone letter, date, latitude and longitude exactly as typed
  on the "Time: ... Date: ... Lat. ... Long. ..." line.
- Copy footnotes (* - Estimates only.) and remarks as typed.
- Mark uncertain characters with ⟦ ⟧, and put your notes on lines starting
  `Flags:` directly under the page they refer to.

The torpedo-data page:
- Read every line left to right and copy the values in the order they are
  typed. Never reorder tube numbers ("#6 #5 #4 #3" stays in that order)
  or the items of a spread ("Middle - Middle - Bow - Stern").
- Keep each tube's value under its tube number, using spaces.
- A value typed once across all the tubes with dashes
  ("- - - Average 130 Port - - - *") is copied once, with its dashes and
  marks. Never split it into one value per tube, and never add a value
  ("None", "No") for a tube where the page has nothing.
- A blank line on the form (e.g. "Actuation Actual:" with nothing after
  it) stays blank.
- When you finish each torpedo page, compare your Tubes Fired line and
  every Serial No. line with the page once more, digit by digit.

RULES
1. Transcribe exactly as typed, including misspellings. Do not add [sic].
   Beware of reading errors: on these carbon copies the typewriter's e, o
   and c look alike, as do 3/8, 5/6 and 1/7. Read each word as a whole.
   When the letters form a real word only one way ("Commenced", not
   "Commonced"; "patrol", not "petrol"), write that word. Keep a
   misspelling only when the letters are clearly legible as typed.
   Numbers can't be read as words: if a digit could be another digit,
   write your best reading in ⟦ ⟧ and flag it.
2. Keep times, zone letters and dates exactly as typed: 1723I 17MAY,
   0310(K) 10/4/43 and 1855 10/3/43 are all fine.
3. Keep positions as typed, including the separator between latitude
   and longitude.
4. If any character is illegible, overstruck or ambiguous, write your
   best reading, wrap it in ⟦ ⟧, and explain in your flags
   (e.g. "⟦5⟧00 — first digit faint, could be blank").
5. Flag internal inconsistencies without fixing them: tonnage that
   doesn't fit the ship category, missing zone letters, more hits than
   torpedoes, and similar.
6. Record the page number typed on each page.
7. Leave blanks blank. Never infer values.
8. Never report what a page "probably" says from other pages, from other
   reports, or from what you know of the war. Only what is on the page.
